marriage.headline: Venus (wife) stands in the 2nd from Jupiter (the native): the next step in the native's affairs; marriage is promised at lesser strength.
notes: Saturn with Venus: the classic delay; marriage tends to come later than the family norm (the delay is sourced; any specific age is provisional).
Ketu in trine to Venus: obstacles before marriage and disputes after it, at trine strength.

children.headline: Venus stands in the 2nd from Jupiter, the putra karaka. This tradition treats the connection as less prominent; it cannot establish a delay or number of children.
notes: The 5th from Jupiter (Gemini) is empty and unaspected in this sign-based calculation; no conclusion about children follows.
Ketu with or in trine to Venus: a traditional family-related link, not evidence of a difficulty.
Saturn with or in trine to Venus: some Nadi readers consider Saturn a timing factor; it does not establish a delay.

lakshmi.headline: Venus in Pisces: 7 of her eight forms stand in this chart — Rajya, Dhanya, Dhairya, Vidya, Santana, Aadi and Dhana Lakshmi, each through its planet's place from Venus.
notes: Each form ripens in the dasha of its planet: the book times its first case to the Rahu mahadasha for Rahu in the 2nd from Venus (p. 173). The dasha years are shown beside each form.

The house sets are broad — four to ten of the twelve houses from Venus qualify for each planet — so most charts carry several forms at once. This is a promise-and-timing reading, not a test; the book's own case 2 reads three forms together (p. 177).
Source: S. Prakash, DNA Astrology of Wealth (2022) — a modern research work on Bhrigu Nandi Nadi, not a classical text. It is read alongside the Rao/Naik combinations, never in their place.

findings.text: Karakamsa in Aquarius: one who builds tanks, wells and public works.
Mars in the Karakamsa: work with metals, chemistry, weapons or fire; an engineering or martial bent.
Mars in the Karakamsa or its 5th: a logician, sharp in argument.
Benefics on the 9th from the Karakamsa: steadfast in dharma, truthful, devoted to elders and teachers.
Ishta devata from the 12th of the Karakamsa (Moon): Gauri.
Planets influencing the 11th from the Arudha lagna are the sources of income: benefics by fair means, malefics by harder or questionable ones. More planets, more gain.
Planets influencing the 12th from the Arudha lagna show where money goes; if more planets touch the 12th than the 11th, spending outruns income.
Rahu on the 7th or 12th from the Arudha lagna: spiritual knowledge and good fortune.
Moon, Jupiter, Mercury or Mars in the 3rd or 11th from the Arudha lagna: many capable siblings.
Benefic on the Upapada: full happiness from the spouse and children.
Benefic on the 2nd from the Upapada: the marriage endures; a fortunate and graceful spouse.
Benefic aspect on the 10th from the Karakamsa: steady purpose in work, not capricious.
Saturn in the 5th or 9th from the Karakamsa: a grip on mantra and the unseen; with benefic company it is turned to helping others (1.2.85).
Expenses flow through the 12th from the Arudha lagna (Rahu): Rahu: penalties, foreigners and unconventional dealings.
Gains flow through the 11th from the Arudha lagna (Moon, Jupiter): Jupiter: taxes, dues and the counsel of the learned; Moon: the public, and a certainty to the outcome.
Arudha lagna in the 4th from the lagna, a kendra: standing and prosperity come readily (1.3.18).
Darapada in a kendra, trikona or upachaya from the lagna: agreement between the partners.
Padas in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the lagna meet obstruction in their matters: A8 longevity in the 12th, A10 career in the 8th.
Argala on the Arudha lagna and its 7th: unobstructed argala brings good fortune; benefic argala brings plenty.

Lords aspecting the lagna and the Atmakaraka's sign: the 4th lord Mercury: contentment and a settled home (1.3.38); the 8th lord Saturn: money is hard to hold (1.3.39); the 12th lord Venus: a free hand with spending (1.3.40).
A2 in Pisces, the 7th from the Arudha lagna, a kendra: savings and family wealth stand behind the public image (Parashara 29.31, 29.37).

classical.text: The Indu Lagna holds benefic Venus together with malefic Sun, Mercury and Saturn: the verse scales the benefic-alone and malefic-only cases, so a mixed sign falls between its tiers.

Jupiter, lord of the Indu Lagna, stands in the 12th from it in Aquarius (neutral): neither IV.11's prosperity clause nor IV.10's destruction clause is cleanly met, so the lord is read mixed (provisional).

findings.text: The Indu Lagna's own lord Jupiter stands in the 12th from it, in Aquarius (neutral), alone.
findings.pages: DNA Astrology of Wealth, case studies pp. 172-249

findings.text: Benefic Venus in the Indu Lagna: the dasha period of this planet gives good results.
The 11th from the Indu Lagna is occupied or aspected by Mars and Rahu: wealth promise, through an unfair medium.
Moon in the 5th, 9th or 11th from the Indu Lagna: the book's second line for becoming wealthy.

notes: Calculation: the 5th from the Moon, from the kalas of the two ninth lords (Saturn 1 from the lagna, Moon 16 from the Moon, sum 17). Uttara Kalamrita IV.27, trans. V. Subrahmanya Sastri (1939), public-domain e-text at astrojyoti.com. The Tamil Jataka Alankaram teaches the same rule.

The DNA Astrology of Wealth book uses this lagna in all twenty-two case studies yet never states the calculation; the reading rules above (2nd and 11th from the Indu Lagna, benefic dashas, the soft planets in 2nd/4th and 5th/9th/11th) are its own, pp. 92-93.

Benefic and malefic follow BPHS 3.11 natural classification (Jupiter and Venus; the waxing Moon; Mercury unless joined by a malefic). "Aspected" means full sign-based graha drishti — the book names no aspect scheme, so that choice is provisional.
The Indu Lagna feeds nothing in the Nadi reading: the systems stay separate, and this panel only reports it.

The Indu Lagna's lord is read in every one of the book's case studies (pp. 172-249) — an empty Indu Lagna is read through it, the way any empty bhava is. The flourishing and destruction conditions come from Uttara Kalamrita IV.10-12, the same text's bhava-lord doctrine seventeen slokas before the Indu Lagna verse (Phaladeepika XV.2-3 agrees, Sastri trans., wisdomlib.org); applying them to the Indu Lagna as the bhava concerned is an extension, so that finding is provisional. Combustion ("eclipsed" in IV.10) is left to the eye: the texts differ on the orbs.
